content.comment_body: Hello programmers, I'm encountering an unusual issue with my [product_name] controllers running [product_name] in a cloud environment. I have four controllers each executing different programs, but typically every 3-4 days, they randomly lose cloud connection (all displayed values drop to zero). This problem occurs at unpredictable times, without any clear pattern. To restore connectivity, I reopen [product_name] and re-upload the same program to AWS, which gives me a working connection for another 3-4 days, and then the issue repeats. During loss of connection through the cloud, I can still observe device shadow values in AWS. I'm certain the controllers remain powered on and connected to the internet at all times. I've also attached images showing the AWS shadow and [product_name] environment.[url] Has anyone else experienced this, or can offer any ideas or solutions?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing a recurring issue where their [product_name] controllers, operating with [product_name] in a cloud setup, intermittently lose cloud connectivity every few days. When this happens, data values in the cloud interface reset to zero, despite the devices staying online and powered. Re-uploading the controller program to AWS temporarily resolves the issue, but it returns after several days, making remote monitoring unreliable and raising concerns about the consistency of the [company_name] cloud solution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable, uninterrupted cloud connectivity for their [product_name] controllers, enabling seamless value reporting and monitoring through [product_name], without having to repeatedly intervene or re-upload programs.
